name: io.github.XGamesFun/solana-kit
title: xsolana
description: Design, check, simulate and review game economies for Solana: a JSON spec, no contract to write.

tools.name: xsolana_guide
tools.description: What an economy on loot can be made of: shops, loot boxes and packs, gacha, lotteries and raffles, auctions (the highest bid wins, the outbid refunded at once), staking and farms, crafting and merging, seasons and emissions, contests players back a side in, quests and airdrops, holder-gated drops, and NFTs of other collections used in a game. loot is one shared Solana program (on devnet, and on mainnet when the spec says "network": "mainnet"; not independently audited): an economy is a JSON spec, not a new smart contract. With no `part`, returns a short index of every part and topic. With a part, returns its fields from the schema, who acts at play time and its nested shapes; with a topic (writing, cheating, asks, cannot), how to write a spec, designing against bots, asks that look impossible, or what loot cannot do and the nearest versions it can.

part.description: One part, with its fields and nested shapes, or one topic (writing, cheating, asks, cannot).

tools.name: xsolana_examples
tools.description: Worked economies to start from. With `query` (a request in its own words), returns the closest worked examples (whole specs that check and go live in the tests), the closest of 112 real or trending economies rated against loot (great / some / a-lot / cannot, with what carries each or what is missing), and what loot can’t do exactly in the request, each with the nearest versions it can. With `name`, returns that example’s whole spec. With neither, lists every example.

query.description: What the person wants, in a few words.

name.description: An example’s name, to get its whole spec.

tools.name: xsolana_check
tools.description: Checks an economy spec. Returns its refusals, each with a code, what it means and its fix, which keep a spec from going live; and its warnings, what the person behind the economy needs to know: chance that pays money, revenue paid to stakers, an unfunded prize, a grant without limits, a mint’s powers, a time far off (with its date in words), a token a player can hold a payment up in, a box longer than one answer of the oracle’s holds. The program refuses only what it must, so much of what a project sets up is accepted with a warning. Also returns how many wallet approvals each action takes. Takes the spec inline (`spec`) or a worked example by name.

spec.description: An economy spec (version 2) given inline. Takes precedence over file and example.

example.description: A worked example by name (stud-farm, nft-raffle, …).

tools.name: xsolana_simulate
tools.description: The quick simulation: expected values from the spec, computed at once. Returns what each box, ticket and craft gives back against its price, what the game keeps, each pool’s money in and out per day and whether it runs dry, settles or grows, farm rewards per unit staked, and what players, the treasury and the platform get each day, at the fees of the economy’s own network; a box’s chances with its odds rules at their most, what a box that gives nothing for a miss misses as its outcomes run out, what a ticket weighs in a lottery weighed by time, and what places get from a pool that starts short. `scenario` overrides the spec’s own ({"perDay": {"box:flip": 1000}, "days": 30, "staked": {"<farm>": 1000}}).

spec.description: An economy spec (version 2) given inline. Takes precedence over file and example.

example.description: A worked example by name (stud-farm, nft-raffle, …).

scenario.description: What to assume in place of the spec’s scenario.

tools.name: xsolana_cost
tools.description: What going live costs (each account’s rent, the program’s fees, network fees, the seeds, the transactions it takes) and what each action costs whoever signs it while it runs, at the fees of the economy’s own network. It prices only: nothing is sent.

spec.description: An economy spec (version 2) given inline. Takes precedence over file and example.

example.description: A worked example by name (stud-farm, nft-raffle, …).

tools.name: xsolana_explain
tools.description: The economy in plain words: what players do and what it costs and is worth, how the pools fill and drain, what runs by itself, what the authority must sign, what going live costs, and what is flagged for the law.

spec.description: An economy spec (version 2) given inline. Takes precedence over file and example.

example.description: A worked example by name (stud-farm, nft-raffle, …).

tools.name: xsolana_review
tools.description: Reviews an economy the way a cheater reads it, before it goes live (a review, not a validity check). For every route that pays or gives value it says who can trigger it, what the program enforces, what it trusts off the chain, and the most one cheater gets; then findings with stable ids and a severity; then, for each grant paid on vouchers, whether its server decides, replays or only bounds the result (its "trust"), what a cheater gets at that level, and what the next level costs to build. Takes the spec inline (`spec`) or a worked example by name. Answers { ok (false when a finding is high, or the spec does not check: then `refusals`), routes: [{ kind ("grant", "farm", "item", "box", "payment", "recipe", "lottery", "contest", "auction", "schedule", "hold", "decision"), key, name, trigger, enforced: [words], trusts: [words], trust ("decides" | "replays" | "bounds" | null), ceiling (words), feeds: ["farm:<key>", …: what its prize is staked in, crafted into or buys] }], findings: [{ id (R-…), severity ("high" | "medium" | "low" | "info"), route ("grant:<key>", "farm:<key>", … or "economy"), message, fix }] }; the trade-offs are in its text.

spec.description: An economy spec (version 2) given inline. Takes precedence over file and example.

example.description: A worked example by name (stud-farm, nft-raffle, …).

tools.name: xsolana_design
tools.description: From what a person wants to the specs that do it, when no single part does it all or the wants pull against each other. Each want is a requirement naming its route (the key of the lottery, item, grant, farm or contest it is about; its family follows from that): a draw ("pay-in" {currencies: [{token, amount}]}, "burn", "refund-as-paid", "free-entry" {grant, perPerson, spendable}, "one-approval", "one-draw", "one-token", "first-reward-no-sol"); a sale of an item ("pay-in", "fixed-price", "instant", "fair-scarce" {perPerson, list}, "one-approval"); a reward, a grant ("per-person" {claims}, "no-server", "bot-proof", "bounded" {total}, "first-reward-no-sol"; a server’s voucher keys as "serverKeys" on any of them); staking, a farm ("emission-cap" {total}, "predictable", "no-lock", "whale-fair"; "perDay" and "days" on any of them); a contest ("no-owner-trust", "equal-stakes" {amount}, "refund-if-no-result"; decider keys as "serverKeys"). Takes the spec as it stands, with each route’s skeleton. For each route it builds every combination of known bridges (an entry token each currency buys, crafted in the purchase; a payment held to the draw; a fixed-price listing in each currency; an allowlist; a deciding voucher server; a fixed or shared rate, minted or from a vault, with an end or a halving; a decider key), checks each, tests every requirement on it, and answers the designs best first (what the person asked for, then how it plays, then how clean, then how secure), with what each keeps (✓), keeps in part (~) and gives up (✗), a sentence for the person and what each needs from them; when none keeps them all, what has to give. Each design’s spec is in `designs`.

spec.description: An economy spec (version 2) given inline. Takes precedence over file and example.

requirements.description: What the person wants, each a requirement the tools can test.

top.description: How many designs to answer (3 by default).

tools.name: xsolana_status
tools.description: A live economy as it is on chain: the project, every pool’s balance, every record the spec names (found or missing). Reads the economy’s own network.

spec.description: An economy spec (version 2) given inline. Takes precedence over file and example.

tools.name: xsolana_token
tools.description: A token made elsewhere, as the chain has it: given its mint’s address, returns its ready `tokens` entry (`source: "existing"`) with its name, ticker, decimals and token program, and `powers`: what the mint’s own keys can do (mint more, freeze, a transfer fee, a transfer hook, a permanent delegate, a pause…), in words too. Reads the cluster this server works on, which its answer names: the mint and its name record only, not the link the record names.

key.description: What the spec will call it (default: its ticker, in the letters a key takes).

project.description: The loot project’s address, when the token is one the project is to mint on a mint of its own: its mint authority then reads as the project’s, or as not handed over yet.

tools.name: xsolana_client
tools.description: How an app (a game, a site, a bot) uses a live economy: the program’s address and cluster, the npm package and IDL, and the calls a page makes with the player’s own wallet (open a box, buy, stake, craft, enter, claim).
